description: Simio is discrete-event simulation software that its maker promotes as an intelligent process digital twin: a virtual replica of operations with continuous, two-way connections to the physical processes, fed with real-time data, used to test what-if scenarios, quantify risk, find bottlenecks and optimise resources before changes are made physically. The product line covers discrete-event simulation, advanced planning and scheduling, demand-driven material requirements planning (DDMRP) and process digital twins, with Python integration, NVIDIA Omniverse visualisation, AI optimisation and a data and integration framework. Simio reports use by Fortune 500 companies across sectors worldwide. Trial, commercial and academic downloads are offered, with an academic programme, Simio University training and case studies; prices are not shown on the home page. Caveats: it is proprietary, and the digital twin claims depend on the integration a user builds. For simulation it models production, logistics and service operations for capacity, scheduling, disruption and contingency planning, and can run as an operational digital twin. Related catalogue records include FlexSim and Siemens Plant Simulation.
